newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnair says to buy 12 Airbus planes.
newsitem.headline: Finnair says to buy 12 Airbus planes.

text.p: Finnish national carrier Finnair Oy's chief executive Antti Potila said on Friday the airline had decided to buy 12 new aircraft from European Airbus Industries.
"We will buy Airbus," Potila told a news conference.
In a statement, Finnair said it would buy the Airbus 320-series and that its initial order for 12 aircraft would include an option for 24 planes more of the same series.
Finnair's choice had been between Airbus and U.S. Boeing.
"The total value of the purchase to be divided over three financial years is about two billion markka," Finnair said.
The exact value of the deal would be clear when Finnair had decided which of the Airbus 320-series' three models -- the 126-seat A319, the 153-seat A320 and the 188-seat A321 -- it would buy.
"The planes of the Airbus 320-family are very well suited for Finnair's traffic," it said in the statement.
Finnair said it expected to have the first two new planes -- both the A321 model -- in traffic at the start of 1999.
